name: Alrumh
description: A star 216 parsecs away, 117 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71995: radius 116.702 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 2193.28 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.091) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71995: effective temperature 3659 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.133)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 71995: distance 215.983 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.06), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 216 parsecs away, 117 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 2,193 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,659 K, so 116.702 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 71995: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: 34 Boötis
quotes.card: 34 Boötis, also named Alrumh, is a single variable star in the northern constellation Boötes, located around 700 light years away from the Sun.
quotes.introduction: At that distance, the visual magnitude of the star is diminished by an extinction of 0.49±0.02 due to interstellar dust.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1279618955326351488 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
